title: First characters of each line
description: Every line of events.log starts with a date written as ten characters (year-month-day). Print just those first ten characters of each line, one date per line, in file order. Nothing else may be printed: no event text, no trailing space.
objective: Practise selecting a range of character positions from every line.
setup:
printf '2026-10-27 deploy started
2026-10-28 cache cleared
2026-10-29 deploy finished
' > events.log
check:
expected='2026-10-27
2026-10-28
2026-10-29'
if [ "$(cat "$CMM_STDOUT")" != "$expected" ]; then
  echo "Expected only the first ten characters of each line, in file order:"
  echo "$expected"
  echo "Got:"
  cat "$CMM_STDOUT"
  exit 1
fi

title: Second field, delimited lines only
description: settings.txt holds key;value pairs separated by a semicolon, mixed with lines that have no semicolon at all. Print the value (the part after the semicolon) of every pair, one per line, in file order. Lines without a semicolon must not appear in the output — by default they would be passed through untouched, so leaving them out has to be asked for explicitly.
objective: Practise picking a field with a custom delimiter while suppressing lines that lack it.
check:
expected='db.local
5432
admin'
if [ "$(cat "$CMM_STDOUT")" != "$expected" ]; then
  echo "Expected only the values of the key;value lines, in file order:"
  echo "$expected"
  echo "Got:"
  cat "$CMM_STDOUT"
  echo "(Lines without a semicolon must be left out, not printed as they are.)"
  exit 1
fi

title: Dropping a field from piped output
description: The executable ./accounts prints colon-separated records of the form name:password:uid:home:shell. Run it and send its output through a pipe into a second command that drops the password field: keep the first field and every field from the third one to the end, still joined by colons. Example: alice:x:1001:/home/alice:/bin/bash -> alice:1001:/home/alice:/bin/bash. Print one record per line, in the original order, and nothing else. The data must arrive through the pipe, not from a file.
objective: Practise combining a single field and an open-ended field range on input read from a pipe.
check:
if ! grep -q '|' "$CMM_COMMAND"; then
  echo "The output of ./accounts has to be piped into the second command."
  exit 1
fi
expected='alice:1001:/home/alice:/bin/bash
bob:1002:/home/bob:/bin/zsh
carol:1003:/srv/carol:/bin/sh'
if [ "$(cat "$CMM_STDOUT")" != "$expected" ]; then
  echo "Expected each record without its password field, colons kept:"
  echo "$expected"
  echo "Got:"
  cat "$CMM_STDOUT"
  exit 1
fi
